items.prompt: White to move. Find the best move.

claims.statement: 24.Rxd4 is legal.
In a four-line search at depth 16 the engine's first choice is Rxd4.
Black's king stands on a7.
A white knight stands on a5.
The white queen stands on f4.
A black pawn stands on c5.
Exactly one black piece attacks d4, where the rook would land (the pawn on c5).
Trading queens with Qxd6 is at least 80 centipawns below the top move.

hints: Count the attackers you can bring near Black's king, then ask which Black pawn or piece stands in the way of more of them.
A rook can take a pawn and then be taken by a pawn. Ask what that pawn leaves behind when it moves.
The pawn on d4 is attacked by the rook on d1, and only the pawn on c5 can take back on d4.
items.explain: In a four-line search (the engine ranks its four best moves at once) at depth 16, the engine puts 24.Rxd4 first. The rook goes to d4, a square attacked by one black piece, the pawn on c5. That is evidence for the game move, not proof that it is the only good one.

feedback_by_move.f4d6: Offering a queen trade is rated clearly lower: at depth 16 the engine puts Qxd6 at least 80 centipawns below 24.Rxd4.

items.prompt: White to move. Find the best move.

claims.statement: 25.Re7+ is legal.
In a four-line search at depth 16 the engine's first choice is Re7+.
The black queen stands on d6.
After Re7 the black queen on d6 attacks the rook.
After Re7 no other white piece defends the rook.
Qxd4+ is at least 200 centipawns below the top move.
Nc6+ is at least 200 centipawns below the top move.

hints: Black's c-pawn has just left c5. List your forcing moves and what each one leaves undefended.
One check puts a rook on a square that the black queen attacks. Ask what the queen would be leaving if it took.
The rook on e1 gives check on the seventh rank.
items.explain: In a four-line search at depth 16 the engine ranks 25.Re7+ first. The rook lands on e7, where the black queen attacks it and no other white piece defends it. The natural-looking 25.Qxd4+ is rated at least 200 centipawns (two pawns) lower.

feedback_by_move.f4d4: Taking the pawn on d4 with check looks natural, but at depth 16 the engine rates Qxd4+ at least 200 centipawns (two pawns) below 25.Re7+.
feedback_by_move.a5c6: Nc6+ is check, but at depth 16 the engine rates it at least 200 centipawns (two pawns) below 25.Re7+.

items.prompt: White to move. Find the best move.

claims.statement: 27.b4+ is legal.
In a four-line search at depth 16 the engine's first choice is b4+.
Black's king stands on a5.
After b4 two white pieces defend the pawn (the pawn on a3 and the queen).
Qc3+ is at least 200 centipawns below the top move.

hints: Black's king has walked to a5. List your forcing moves.
A king cannot take a pawn that another piece defends. Which pawn check would be defended?
The pawn on b2 moves to b4.
items.explain: In a four-line search at depth 16 the engine ranks 27.b4+ first. After the pawn move two white pieces defend b4, the pawn on a3 and the queen. The queen check 27.Qc3+ is rated at least 200 centipawns (two pawns) lower.

feedback_by_move.d4c3: A queen check also looks forcing, but at depth 16 the engine rates Qc3+ at least 200 centipawns (two pawns) below 27.b4+.

items.prompt: White to move. Find the best move.

claims.statement: 36.Bf1 is legal.
In a four-line search at depth 16 the engine's first choice is Bf1.
The black queen stands on c4.
After Bf1 one white piece (the bishop) attacks the queen on c4.
After Bf1 one black piece (the pawn on b5) defends the queen on c4.
Rc7 is at least 500 centipawns below the top move.
Qa3 is at least 500 centipawns below the top move.

hints: Checks are not the only forcing moves. List the moves that attack a piece, and see which attacked pieces are defended.
The queen on c4 is defended by a pawn, so an attack on it makes Black decide something. Which of your pieces can attack it quietly?
The bishop on h3 goes back to f1.
items.explain: In a four-line search at depth 16 the engine ranks 36.Bf1 first; the next moves it lists are far lower (Rc7 and Qa3 are each at least 500 centipawns, five pawns, below it). After Bf1 one white piece, the bishop, attacks the queen on c4, and one black piece, the pawn on b5, defends it.

feedback_by_move.b7c7: At depth 16 the engine rates Rc7 at least 500 centipawns (five pawns) below 36.Bf1.
feedback_by_move.b2a3: At depth 16 the engine rates Qa3 at least 500 centipawns (five pawns) below 36.Bf1.

items.prompt: White to move. Find the best move.

claims.statement: 37.Rd7 is legal.
37.Bxc4 is legal.
In a four-line search at depth 16 the engine's first choice is Rd7.
The black queen stands on c4.
Only the bishop on f1 attacks the queen on c4.
The black rook on d2 attacks the white queen on b2.

hints: Before you decide what to take, list what each Black piece attacks.
The rook on d2 attacks your queen on b2. Is there a move that deals with that rook first?
The rook on b7 goes to d7, where the black rook can take it.
items.explain: In a four-line search at depth 16 the engine ranks 37.Rd7 first. The queen on c4 can be taken by the bishop, but the black rook on d2 attacks your queen on b2, so the capture is not simply free: after 37.Bxc4 Rxb2+ 38.Kxb2 bxc4 each side keeps a rook.

feedback_by_move.f1c4: Bxc4 takes the queen, but the black rook on d2 then takes your queen on b2. In a four-line search at depth 16 the engine ranks 37.Rd7 first.
